question: Can the pinned public Qwen3.5-2B Q4_K_M artifact complete the canonical Android campaign through public llama.cpp OpenCL offload on the Galaxy S23 Ultra Adreno 740?

scope.included: Text-only inference using the same pinned Unsloth GGUF through llama.cpp GPUOpenCL0 / Adreno 740 with all 25 model layers requested for offload.
excluded: GPU-exclusive claims: CPU orchestration and unsupported OpenCL operations remain in bounds and disclosed

upstream_model.name: Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B
upstream_model.architecture: 24-layer dense hybrid: three Gated DeltaNet layers followed by one full-attention layer, repeated six times
upstream_model.source: Pinned official model card and config.json. The official repository is Transformers-format source, not the deployed Android artifact.

deployment_artifact.source_kind: third-party GGUF conversion and quantization derived from Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B
deployment_artifact.format: GGUF v3, one self-contained shard, text model only

quantization.name: Q4_K_M
quantization.weight_scheme: GGML K-quant medium: primarily Q4_K block quantization with the Q4_K_M mixed tensor policy
quantization.block_scheme: Q4_K uses 256-weight super-blocks composed of 32-weight blocks with quantized scales/minima; the M variant retains selected tensors at higher precision according to the quantizer policy.
quantization.conversion_tool_revision_missing_reason: The pinned Unsloth repository and GGUF metadata identify Unsloth, Q4_K_M, and the importance matrix but do not publish the exact converter/quantizer commit. Artifact bytes are still bound by revision, size, and SHA-256; this provenance limitation must remain visible.

tokenizer_and_template.template_difference: The deployed template changes only iteration over tool-call argument mappings. The canonical system+user, no-tools branch is unaffected; canonical rendered bytes are independently hash-bound.

thinking.proof:
Every canonical rendered prompt must end with the exact bytes <think>

</think>

. A nonempty thinking prefix is a fatal mismatch.

route_rationale.chosen: After the same-device Vulkan shader pipeline proved durably blocked, upstream llama.cpp issue #19746 reported OpenCL working on Adreno 740. The pinned llama.cpp revision already includes a public OpenCL backend designed first for Qualcomm Adreno, Q4_K/Q5_K support, Adreno 7xx detection, embedded source kernels, and Qwen3.5 gated-delta-net kernels.
route_rationale.revision_difference: None: the same llama.cpp commit used for CPU and Vulkan is retained, avoiding a silent runtime revision change.
route_rationale.offload_claim_boundary: GPU offload requires OpenCL platform selection, an Adreno 740 device, 25/25 layers offloaded, and OpenCL model and compute buffers in the same server log. CPU retains server/tokenizer/sampler/scheduler orchestration and operations unsupported by OpenCL; this is not GPU-exclusive.
route_rationale.fallback_policy: Missing device/buffer/layer proof, an ignored GPU request, unsupported device, OpenCL build error, or CPU-only route is blocked evidence, not a GPU result.

runtime.name: llama.cpp

opencl_link_loader.deployment: Link-only artifact, never deployed. Android resolves DT_NEEDED libOpenCL.so to the authorized phone vendor implementation.

kernel_sources.embedding: All listed OpenCL C kernel sources and embed_kernel.py are embedded in the executable; the phone vendor driver compiles them during route setup.

runtime.build: CMake Release, GGML_OPENCL=ON, OpenCL target 3.0, embedded source kernels, Adreno optimized kernels enabled, restricted binary kernel library disabled; static llama/GGML and c++_static. Source/build paths prefix-mapped; web UI and OpenSSL disabled.
runtime.greedy_proof: Same pinned llama.cpp temperature=-1 argmax path as 0027.
runtime.state_reset: One loaded server/slot; separately timed POST /slots/0?action=erase; cache_prompt=false; require cache_n=0, full prompt_n, positive prompt_ms.

device.phone_lock: artifacts/locks/phone.lock held across identity, staging, execution, evidence, and cleanup

timing_and_evidence.setup_boundary: Immediately before server launch through health plus required OpenCL backend proof; includes vendor kernel compilation, model mapping/offload, context and initial KV allocation.
timing_and_evidence.request_boundary: Immediately before native template rendering through final streamed stop delivery. The separately timed slot erase completes before this boundary and is not included in total request.
timing_and_evidence.request_to_first_token: Client request start through the first SSE event carrying a generated token ID.
timing_and_evidence.prefill: llama.cpp final-event prompt_ms and prompt_n; route-internal prompt evaluation timing.
timing_and_evidence.post_prefill_to_first_token: Null because llama.cpp does not expose a server-clock first-token timestamp alignable with aggregate prompt_ms.
timing_and_evidence.decode: External first generated-token event through final stop event, with the first token excluded from the numerator; llama.cpp predicted timing is retained separately and includes all generated tokens.
timing_and_evidence.memory: 100 ms target process PSS/VmHWM plus public KGSL busy/frequency sampling. Process PSS does not isolate vendor driver/GPU-private allocations.

fatal_gates: missing OpenCL Adreno 740 device, 25/25 layer offload, OpenCL model buffer, or OpenCL compute buffer proof
GPU option ignored, unsupported OpenCL device, OpenCL kernel build failure, or CPU-only fallback

viability_smoke.classification: provider-bound one-request milestone only; not canonical benchmark evidence

nullable_not_fatal: KGSL telemetry when server OpenCL proof is complete
brief memory/activity peaks missed by sampling
exact individual-op OpenCL/CPU split when claim remains bounded GPU offload
